title: H2-LLM: Hardware-Dataflow Co-Exploration for Heterogeneous Hybrid-Bonding-based Low-Batch LLM Inference
problem: Edge-side low-batch LLM inference (personal assistant, reception bot, private edge server) is bottlenecked by the DRAM bandwidth wall: existing NMP designs embed compute engines inside DRAM dies, limiting compute capacity and creating an imbalance between bandwidth and computation for both prefill (compute-bound) and decoding (bandwidth-bound) stages. Hybrid-bonding technology offers a path to higher compute capacity near memory, but the trade-off between computation capacity and bandwidth has not been systematically explored.
motivation: Low-batch LLM inference at the edge is memory-bandwidth-bound during decoding and requires a near-memory heterogeneous architecture; hybrid bonding (face-to-face die stacking) enables significantly more compute logic near memory than in-die NMP, but maximizing efficiency requires co-optimizing the architecture and dataflow simultaneously.
method: H2-LLM proposes a hybrid-bonding-based heterogeneous accelerator that places high-capacity compute dies in face-to-face contact with DRAM dies, exploiting the high through-silicon-via bandwidth of hybrid bonding. The architecture exposes a design space covering compute tile counts, memory bandwidth allocation, and die partitioning. A data-centric dataflow abstraction is introduced to map LLM operations (attention, feed-forward, KV-cache access) onto the heterogeneous on-die and near-die compute resources across both prefill and decoding stages. A design space exploration (DSE) framework automatically searches this joint architecture-dataflow space for the Pareto-optimal configuration.
key_novelty: H2-LLM is the first system to jointly explore the hardware architecture and dataflow design space for hybrid-bonding-based heterogeneous LLM accelerators, using a data-centric dataflow abstraction that maximally exploits the heterogeneous compute and bandwidth resources.
contributions: A hybrid-bonding-based heterogeneous accelerator architecture for low-batch edge LLM inference with explicit architecture design space characterization.
A data-centric dataflow abstraction that maps prefill and decoding LLM operations across heterogeneous on-die and near-die compute resources.
An automated DSE framework that jointly searches the architecture and dataflow design space to find the optimal configuration.
2.72x geomean speedup and 1.48x geomean energy efficiency improvement over in-die NMP-based heterogeneous accelerators.

metrics.speedup: 2.72x geomean over in-die NMP-based heterogeneous accelerators
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.48x geomean better energy efficiency vs in-die NMP baseline

limitations: Not discussed; thermal and manufacturing yield implications of hybrid bonding at scale are not evaluated.
primary_theme: Hybrid-bonding heterogeneous architecture and dataflow co-exploration for edge LLM inference
